title: Simulator rig with racing seat, three curved monitors and camera/lens assembly
objects_and_counts: No people are visible in the photographed scene.
One racing-style bucket seat is visible in the left foreground; the seat shows a fabric cushion and a glossy hard outer shell and is not cropped.

Three large curved monitors are visible across the top of the image (top-center to top-right); two form a continuous curved bank at the right and one is centered-left. All three monitor faces are visible and mounted on a frame.
One computer keyboard is visible behind the seat, resting on the rig work surface (top-center area).
One camera or box-shaped imaging device with a mounted lens is visible on the rig, located center-right on a linear rail/beam; the lens and camera body are not cropped.
One vertical handbrake-style lever is visible just left of the camera assembly (center-right).
One short gearstick or joystick with a spherical ball top is visible center-left on a small rectangular base.
Two stacked flight-case style road cases (aluminium-reinforced) are visible on the right side of the image, one above the other.
One retail-style cardboard box with red and white graphics is visible behind the seat at left; the box is partially visible (left background) and slightly cropped by the image edge.
One desktop computer tower or large chassis with visible case fans and internal lighting is visible behind the seat (center-left, slightly obscured by the seat).
Multiple bundled cables and wiring are visible beneath and around the rig and camera assembly (center and lower center); these are numerous and partly obscured by structural elements.
One small silver/grey audio or electronic device (rectangular box) is visible on top of the flight cases at right.
visible_text: WORLD UPDATE : FRANCE, BELGIUM, NETHERLANDS & LUXEMBOURG
WORLD UPDATE : GERMANY, AUSTRIA AND SWITZERLAND
spatial_relations: The racing seat is positioned in the left foreground facing right/toward the monitors and rig.
The three curved monitors are mounted together along the top of the rig, spanning from top-center to top-right; the camera/lens assembly sits directly beneath the central/right monitor area.
The keyboard is located behind the seat on the rig surface, between the seat and the camera assembly (top-center).
The vertical handbrake lever is mounted to the rig immediately left of the camera assembly (center-right).
The small gearstick/joystick with the spherical ball top is mounted on a small rectangular base positioned slightly left of the camera assembly (center-left of the rig).
Two stacked aluminium-reinforced flight cases are placed to the right of the main rig, with a small silver/grey box resting on top of them (right side).
The red and white retail box is located behind the left side of the seat, against the left background.
Cables run beneath and around the linear aluminium beams that form the rig; many cables cluster beneath the camera and to the lower center area.
colours_and_materials: The racing seat has a black fabric cushion and a glossy black rigid outer shell.
The rig framing appears to be made of black anodized aluminium extrusion (T-slot style) with visible black metal connectors.
The monitors have black bezels and dark display surfaces; one monitor shows a blue/teal user interface on-screen.
The flight cases are black with silver aluminium edges and corner reinforcements.
A retail cardboard box at left has dominant red and white printed graphics.
The small silver/grey electronic box on the flight cases is metallic or painted in a light silver colour.
uncertainties: The exact number of monitors could be interpreted differently because two curved panels form a continuous bank at the right and a third is centered to the left; counts above reflect visible distinct screens but mounting could make identification ambiguous.
The small text on the chair emblem and some smaller labels are partially obscured; 'AUTO IMAGE' is legible but a smaller emblem text adjacent to it is unclear.
The retail box text and graphics at left are partially cropped by the image edge and some printed words are unreadable; a single [unreadable] placeholder above indicates additional unreadable text.
Some smaller labels, model numbers or nameplates on the camera body, the silver box on the flight cases, and on cables are not legible in this view.
The presence or identity of pedals or further control assemblies below the rig cannot be determined from this image because that area is obscured by the seat and wiring.
